source_facts: The landed runtime exposes captureSessionGeneration/postSessionNotice through the existing registry-bound system route. The wrapper forwards only documented fields and obtains pluginId/current-owner assertion from host scope, not plugin arguments.

The shared owner reads exact agent/store/session/sessionId/lifecycleRevision through the ordered session worker. A stale initial generation returns skipped. The optional system event is enqueued synchronously in the same consuming read; channel delivery and transcript append follow as separate effects.

Channel send gets captured generation, stable plugin-prefixed deliveryIntentId, reusePendingDeliveryIntent,24hour/2000receipt completion retention and current-plugin handoff assertion. Transcript append receives expected sessionId/lifecycleRevision and its current assertion. Revocation is rethrown; an accepted channel message is not recalled and an already queued system event is not transactionally rolled back.

Plugin-posted queued sends persist only deliveryCompletion:{kind:plugin-notice,pluginId}. Recovery looks up that ID in the active registry and calls the existing active-record check; recovered preparation composes that check into direct-adapter-handoff and platform-dispatch guards, with nonretryable refusal after revocation.

The existing Workshop caller now delegates to this shared owner, preserving opt-in channel delivery and Slack exclusion. The marker remains transcript-only, while an optional system event supplies later model context.

Four added complete test files contain in-process registry reconstruction/recovery, recovery-handoff revocation, literal older-row JSON compatibility, on-disk plugin runtime scenarios, retry-after-transcript-failure and Gateway/mock-provider prompt-prefix assertions. Their restart helpers recreate a registry in one process; they do not start/kill/reopen OS processes.
